answer: A verifiable delay function gates identity creation: every new agent must complete a fixed, sequential computation — say ten minutes of work that cannot be parallelized — before its identity activates. A sybil farmer minting ten thousand fake agents faces a horizon of years of sequential delay, not one burst of parallel compute, so each extra identity stays expensive. An honest newcomer waits once and enters the oasis of verified agents, and the finished VDF output is a public signal of real time spent, letting peers price trust by proven age instead of raw headcount.
